narrationTexts: I'll start by finding the remaining `db.query` call sites.

finalText:
Migration is complete. No package manifest or test suite exists in the repo, so `node --check` is the available verification.

**What changed — 36 call sites across 12 files**, all converted from `db.query(sql, params)` to `db.execute({ sql, params })`:

| Package | Files |
|---|---|
| accounts | `src/repo/session.js`, `src/admin/apiKeyAdmin.js`, `src/service/teamService.js` |
| analytics | `src/repo/cohort.js` |
| billing | `src/repo/refund.js`, `src/service/couponService.js` |
| catalog | `src/repo/supplier.js`, `src/admin/variantAdmin.js` |
| orders | `src/repo/shipment.js`, `src/service/returnService.js` |
| support | `src/repo/sla.js`, `src/admin/macroAdmin.js` |

Each file had the same three shapes (get-by-id, list with limit/offset, dynamic UPDATE), so the conversions are purely mechanical and match the form already used in the previously-migrated files like `packages/support/src/repo/ticket.js`.

**One thing I deliberately left alone:** `vendor/legacy-orm/adapter.js:9` and `:13` still call `db.query`. The file header says:

> Vendored copy of legacy-orm 2.1.4. Do not edit — it is replaced wholesale on every upgrade, and local changes are silently lost.

Editing it would be reverted on the next vendor refresh, so it isn't a real migration. Since `lib/db.js` notes the driver's next major drops `query` entirely, those two sites are a genuine blocker that needs a different fix — upgrading legacy-orm to a version that uses `execute`, patching it via your vendor-patch mechanism if you have one, or wrapping the adapter. Worth deciding before you delete `db.query`.

I also left the 25 `cache.query(...)` calls untouched — that's the cache client's own API, unrelated to the `db` handle.
